key_insight: TWICE forecast ICU outcomes comparably to task-specific models, but its treatment-response forecasts did not reliably distinguish corrective from opposite treatments.
clinical_relevance: Generative EHR models could support patient-specific ICU forecasting, but these findings do not establish reliable treatment guidance.
method: Trained a 79M-parameter decoder-only transformer to continue ICU electronic health records.
Estimated 19 outcome risks from 50 simulated futures without task-specific training.
Evaluated record fidelity, patient trajectories and counterfactual treatment responses.
evidence_signal: Trained on 127,332 patients and 1.57 billion tokens from one academic health system, TWICE achieved mean held-out AUROC 0.836 versus 0.834 for the best of 144 supervised configurations.
watch_item: Opposite treatments shifted forecasts similarly to corrective treatments on targeted clinical values, limiting confidence in causal treatment-response simulation.
paper_title: Toward a digital twin of the ICU patient: Forecasting and treatment response in a generative event model
